entities.summary: Piero Manzoni di Chiosca e Poggiolo was an Italian artist best known for his ironic approach to avant-garde art. Often compared to the work of Yves Klein, his own work anticipated, and directly influenced, the work of a generation of younger Italian artists brought together by the critic Germano Celant in the first Arte Povera exhibition held in Genoa, 1967. Manzoni is most famous for a series of artworks that call into question the nature of the art object, directly prefiguring Conceptual Art. His work eschews normal artist's materials, instead using everything from rabbit fur to human excrement in order to "tap mythological sources and to realize authentic and universal values".

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Piero Manzoni's innovative approach to art challenged traditional notions of the art object, influencing a generation of conceptual artists and contributing to the development of Arte Povera. His use of unconventional materials in artworks such as 'Artist's Shit' (1961) tapped into mythological sources and questioned the nature of value in art.
